q: 我打算在这家健身房练___，然后再换一家。
zh: 我打算在这家健身房练三个月，然后再换一家。
py: wǒ dǎ suàn zài zhè jiā jiàn shēn fáng liàn sān gè yuè rán hòu zài huàn yī jiā
en: I plan to train at this gym for three months and then switch to another one.
why: How long I train is a length, written 三个月 with 个, and it follows 练. 三月 is the month of March and cannot be the amount of training.

q: 为了退这双鞋，我白跑了两___商场，店员都不在。
zh: 为了退这双鞋，我白跑了两趟商场，店员都不在。
py: wèi le tuì zhè shuāng xié wǒ bái pǎo le liǎng tàng shāng chǎng diàn yuán dōu bú zài
en: To return these shoes I made two wasted trips to the mall, and the staff weren't there.
why: 白跑两趟 counts journeys there and back to the mall. 顿 counts meals, 场 counts events and 个 cannot count trips.

s: 我在这个城市住了三月，然后换了工作。
s_py: wǒ zài zhè ge chéng shì zhù le sān yuè rán hòu huàn le gōng zuò
zh: 我在这个城市住了三个月，然后换了工作。
py: wǒ zài zhè ge chéng shì zhù le sān gè yuè rán hòu huàn le gōng zuò
en: I lived in this city for three months and then changed jobs.
why: 三月 is March, a point in time. A length of time is 三个月, and 月 always needs 个 when counting.

s: 教练教了小李两年网球。
zh: 教练教了小李两年网球。
py: jiào liàn jiāo le xiǎo lǐ liǎng nián wǎng qiú
en: The coach taught Xiao Li tennis for two years.
why: Correct. The person 小李 follows 教了 before the duration, and 网球 closes the sentence. The learner may expect the duration right after 教了.

s: 我听了音乐两个小时。
s_py: wǒ tīng le yīn yuè liǎng gè xiǎo shí
zh: 我听了两个小时音乐。
py: wǒ tīng le liǎng gè xiǎo shí yīn yuè
en: I listened to music for two hours.
why: The duration goes between 听了 and the object. 听了音乐两个小时 keeps the English order and is not Chinese.

s: 这家球馆开业三年了，生意一直不错。
zh: 这家球馆开业三年了，生意一直不错。
py: zhè jiā qiú guǎn kāi yè sān nián le shēng yi yī zhí bú cuò
en: This sports hall has been open for three years, and business has always been good.
why: Correct. 开业 starts at one moment, so the time since follows it and ends in 了.

q: 我下午要去一___超市，你要买什么吗？
zh: 我下午要去一趟超市，你要买什么吗？
py: wǒ xià wǔ yào qù yī tàng chāo shì nǐ yào mǎi shén me ma
en: I need to make a trip to the supermarket this afternoon. Do you need anything?
why: 去一趟 counts a trip there and back. 遍 means doing something through from beginning to end, 场 counts events and 顿 counts meals or scoldings.

s: 这个星期我去了三趟超市，每次都忘了买盐。
zh: 这个星期我去了三趟超市，每次都忘了买盐。
py: zhè gè xīng qī wǒ qù le sān tàng chāo shì měi cì dōu wàng le mǎi yán
en: I've been to the supermarket three times this week and each time forgot to buy salt.
why: Correct. 趟 counts trips there and back, placed after 去了 and before the place 超市.

s: 我在门口等了半天他。
s_py: wǒ zài mén kǒu děng le bàn tiān tā
zh: 我在门口等了他半天。
py: wǒ zài mén kǒu děng le tā bàn tiān
en: I waited for him at the door for ages.
why: A pronoun object goes between the verb and the duration: 等了他半天. 等了半天他 reverses them.

q: 太累了，我们在咖啡馆坐___吧，然后再逛。
zh: 太累了，我们在咖啡馆坐一会儿吧，然后再逛。
py: tài lèi le wǒ men zài kā fēi guǎn zuò yī huì r ba rán hòu zài guàng
en: We're tired. Let's sit in the café for a while and then keep shopping.
why: 一会儿 is a short length of time and follows the verb. 一点儿 means a small amount, and 一次 / 一遍 count occasions, so none of them says how long we sit.

q: 请等___，我马上给您找零钱。
zh: 请等一下，我马上给您找零钱。
py: qǐng děng yī xià wǒ mǎ shàng gěi nín zhǎo líng qián
en: Please wait a moment. I'll get your change right away.
why: 等一下 is the polite 'for a moment'. 一遍 means once through, 一趟 a round trip and 一场 an event, and none of them can follow 等.

q: 我昨天在商店逛___两个小时。
zh: 我昨天在商店逛了两个小时。
py: wǒ zuó tiān zài shāng diàn guàng le liǎng gè xiǎo shí
en: I wandered around the store for two hours yesterday.
why: A finished stretch of time follows the verb, with 了 between the verb and the duration. 过 would claim a life experience, which clashes with the specific day 昨天.

zh: 他星期六在家睡了十个小时。
py: tā xīng qī liù zài jiā shuì le shí gè xiǎo shí
en: He slept for ten hours at home on Saturday.
why: 星期六 is the point in time and goes before the verb phrase; 十个小时 is the length and follows 睡了. They cannot swap places.

src_py: wǒ qù guo nà jiā shāng chǎng
task: Say you have been there twice.
zh: 我去过两次那家商场。
py: wǒ qù guo liǎng cì nà jiā shāng chǎng
en: I've been to that mall twice.
why: With a place object the count may go before or after it; either way it stays after 去过.

q: 店员又把价格说了一___，我才听清楚。
zh: 店员又把价格说了一遍，我才听清楚。
py: diàn yuán yòu bǎ jià gé shuō le yī biàn wǒ cái tīng qīng chu
en: The clerk said the price once more, and only then did I hear it clearly.
why: 说一遍 means saying the whole thing through once more, which is exactly what repeating a price is. 顿 counts meals, 趟 trips and 场 events.

zh: 球迷们已经在门口等了四十分钟了。
py: qiú mí men yǐ jīng zài mén kǒu děng le sì shí fēn zhōng le
en: The fans have already been waiting at the gate for forty minutes.
why: 已经 and 在门口 both come before 等了; 四十分钟 follows it and the final 了 closes the sentence.

q: 在球场上我见过___，他很高。
zh: 在球场上我见过他一次，他很高。
py: zài qiú chǎng shàng wǒ jiàn guo tā yī cì tā hěn gāo
en: I've met him once on the court, and he's tall.
why: A pronoun object goes before the count: 见过他一次. With 他, putting 一次 first is the typical learner error, and 一次的他 is not possible.

zh: 我等了她二十分钟。
py: wǒ děng le tā èr shí fēn zhōng
en: I waited for her for twenty minutes.
why: The pronoun 她 comes right after 等了, before the duration. 二十分钟她 would be the English order.

s: 我两个小时就逛完了所有的商店。
zh: 我两个小时就逛完了所有的商店。
py: wǒ liǎng gè xiǎo shí jiù guàng wán le suǒ yǒu de shāng diàn
en: It took me only two hours to go round all the shops.
why: Correct. With 就 and a result 完, a duration before the verb means 'within that time', a separate pattern from how long an action lasts.

s: 他打网球了两个小时。
s_py: tā dǎ wǎng qiú le liǎng gè xiǎo shí
zh: 他打了两个小时网球。
py: tā dǎ le liǎng gè xiǎo shí wǎng qiú
en: He played tennis for two hours.
why: 了 belongs right after the verb 打, and the duration follows it before the object. 打网球了两个小时 puts 了 after the object.

zh: 我们看了两个小时比赛了。
py: wǒ men kàn le liǎng gè xiǎo shí bǐ sài le
en: We've been watching the match for two hours now.
why: The first 了 follows the verb, the duration sits before the object, and the second 了 closes the sentence to show it is still going on.

q: 她每个星期六都去健身房练___。
zh: 她每个星期六都去健身房练两个小时。
py: tā měi gè xīng qī liù dōu qù jiàn shēn fáng liàn liǎng gè xiǎo shí
en: Every Saturday she works out at the gym for two hours.
why: A habit takes no 了 but the length still follows the verb. 两点 is a clock time, not something you can train for, and a length uses 两 (两个小时), never 二.

zh: 弟弟两个星期没去游泳了。
py: dì di liǎng gè xīng qī méi qù yóu yǒng le
en: My younger brother hasn't been swimming for two weeks.
why: 两个星期 stands before 没 and the sentence ends in 了. The duration cannot follow 游泳 because nothing happened to measure.

zh: 我打了两年网球。
py: wǒ dǎ le liǎng nián wǎng qiú
en: I played tennis for two years.
why: The duration goes between 打了 and the object. 打了网球两年 is the English order and does not work.

q: 去年他在这家球馆打了半年工___，后来去别的城市了。
zh: 去年他在这家球馆打了半年工，后来去别的城市了。
py: qù nián tā zài zhè jiā qiú guǎn dǎ le bàn nián gōng hòu lái qù bié de chéng shì le
en: Last year he worked at this sports hall for half a year, and then he went to another city.
why: 去年 and 后来 place the half year firmly in the past, so only the single 了 after the verb is used. A final 了 would mean he is still working there now.

zh: 她买衣服买了三个小时了。
py: tā mǎi yī fu mǎi le sān gè xiǎo shí le
en: She has been shopping for clothes for three hours now.
why: In the verb-copy form 了 goes on the second verb, and the final 了 shows the shopping is still going on.

q: 我在商场里找了___，你去哪儿了？
zh: 我在商场里找了你一个小时，你去哪儿了？
py: wǒ zài shāng chǎng lǐ zhǎo le nǐ yī gè xiǎo shí nǐ qù nǎ r le
en: I looked for you in the mall for an hour. Where did you go?
why: With the pronoun 你, the order is verb + 了 + pronoun + duration. Both options that start with 一个小时 put the duration before the pronoun, which fails.

q: 他___去买球鞋，在店里试了半个小时。
zh: 他星期六去买球鞋，在店里试了半个小时。
py: tā xīng qī liù qù mǎi qiú xié zài diàn lǐ shì le bàn gè xiǎo shí
en: He went to buy sports shoes on Saturday and spent half an hour trying them on in the shop.
why: 星期六 is a day (when), so it sits before the verb. 六个星期 is a length of six weeks and cannot say when he went.

q: 他___了，现在饿坏了。
zh: 他一天没吃饭了，现在饿坏了。
py: tā yī tiān méi chī fàn le xiàn zài è huài le
en: He hasn't eaten for a whole day, and now he's starving.
why: The period of not doing something goes BEFORE 没 + verb, with 了 at the end. 没吃一天饭 leaves the duration after the verb, where there is no action to measure.

s: 我在商场遇到过一次她。
s_py: wǒ zài shāng chǎng yù dào guo yī cì tā
zh: 我在商场遇到过她一次。
py: wǒ zài shāng chǎng yù dào guo tā yī cì
en: I've run into her once in the mall.
why: With a pronoun object the count comes after it: 遇到过她一次. 一次她 reverses the order.

src_py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn qiú sài
task: Say you watched for three hours, repeating the verb.
zh: 我昨天看球赛看了三个小时。
py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn qiú sài kàn le sān gè xiǎo shí
en: I watched the match for three hours yesterday.
why: To add a duration to verb + object, repeat the verb: 看球赛看了三个小时. 了 goes on the second 看.

src: 我用这部手机用了三年。
src_py: wǒ yòng zhè bù shǒu jī yòng le sān nián
task: Say you have used it for three years and still do.
zh: 我用这部手机用了三年了。
py: wǒ yòng zhè bù shǒu jī yòng le sān nián le
en: I've been using this phone for three years now.
why: In the verb-copy form the second 了 goes at the very end, after the duration, to show it continues.

zh: 他加入这支球队三年了。
py: tā jiā rù zhè zhī qiú duì sān nián le
en: He has been on this team for three years.
why: 加入 happens in an instant, so the time since then follows the object and the sentence ends in 了. The duration cannot come between 加入 and 这支球队.

zh: 我们在球场只见过一次面。
py: wǒ men zài qiú chǎng zhǐ jiàn guo yī cì miàn
en: We've only met once, at the court.
why: 见面 splits around the count, so 见过一次面. The count must stand between 见过 and 面.

s: 我没买一年衣服了。
s_py: wǒ méi mǎi yī nián yī fu le
zh: 我一年没买衣服了。
py: wǒ yī nián méi mǎi yī fu le
en: I haven't bought clothes for a year.
why: The period of not buying goes before 没: 一年没买衣服了. 没买一年衣服 leaves a duration after a verb that never happened.

s: 比赛七点开始，大概打一个半小时。
zh: 比赛七点开始，大概打一个半小时。
py: bǐ sài qī diǎn kāi shǐ dà gài dǎ yī gè bàn xiǎo shí
en: The match starts at seven and lasts about an hour and a half.
why: Correct. 七点 is the start time, before the verb; 一个半小时 is the length and follows 打.

src: 他们打篮球打了一个晚上。
src_py: tā men dǎ lán qiú dǎ le yī gè wǎn shang
task: Say it without repeating the verb.
zh: 他们打了一个晚上篮球。
py: tā men dǎ le yī gè wǎn shang lán qiú
en: They played basketball all evening.
why: Without repeating the verb, the duration is placed between 打了 and the object.

s: 这部电影我看了两趟。
s_py: zhè bù diàn yǐng wǒ kàn le liǎng tàng
zh: 这部电影我看了两遍。
py: zhè bù diàn yǐng wǒ kàn le liǎng biàn
en: I've watched this film twice.
why: 遍 counts viewing something through from start to finish. 趟 counts trips, so 两趟 is wrong with 看.

zh: 我在商店见过他一次。
py: wǒ zài shāng diàn jiàn guo tā yī cì
en: I've met him once in the shop.
why: The pronoun 他 comes before the count: 见过他一次. 见过一次他 is the typical error.

q: 我在体育馆问过___，他都说不认识你。
zh: 我在体育馆问过他两次，他都说不认识你。
py: wǒ zài tǐ yù guǎn wèn guo tā liǎng cì tā dōu shuō bú rèn shi nǐ
en: I've asked him twice at the gym, and he said both times that he doesn't know you.
why: The pronoun 他 comes right after 问过 and before the count: 问过他两次. 问过两次他 is the typical error with a pronoun object.

q: 这份说明书我从头到尾看了三___，还是不会用。
zh: 这份说明书我从头到尾看了三遍，还是不会用。
py: zhè fèn shuō míng shū wǒ cóng tóu dào wěi kàn le sān biàn hái shi bú huì yòng
en: I read the instructions through from start to finish three times and I still can't use it.
why: 从头到尾 signals reading the whole thing through, which is counted with 遍. 趟 counts trips, 下 is a quick light action and 场 counts events.

s: 他已经试了十分钟了衣服，还没出来。
s_py: tā yǐ jīng shì le shí fēn zhōng le yī fu hái méi chū lái
zh: 他已经试了十分钟衣服了，还没出来。
py: tā yǐ jīng shì le shí fēn zhōng yī fu le hái méi chū lái
en: He has been trying on clothes for ten minutes already and hasn't come out.
why: The second 了 goes at the end of the clause, after the object 衣服. Placed between the duration and the object it is wrong.

q: 我们___去体育馆，打了两个小时篮球，才回家。
zh: 我们下午四点去体育馆，打了两个小时篮球，才回家。
py: wǒ men xià wǔ sì diǎn qù tǐ yù guǎn dǎ le liǎng gè xiǎo shí lán qiú cái huí jiā
en: We went to the gym at four in the afternoon, played basketball for two hours, and only then went home.
why: The start time is a point (下午四点) and goes before 去; the two hours of play are a length after 打了. A length like 四个小时 cannot say when we set off.

zh: 他今年去过两次上海。
py: tā jīn nián qù guo liǎng cì shàng hǎi
en: He has been to Shanghai twice this year.
why: A place name allows both orders after 去过: 两次上海 and 上海两次. 今年 is the time frame and stays before the verb.

q: 我们___去超市，大概逛一个小时。
zh: 我们三点去超市，大概逛一个小时。
py: wǒ men sān diǎn qù chāo shì dà gài guàng yī gè xiǎo shí
en: We're going to the supermarket at three, and we'll browse for about an hour.
why: The time we GO is a point in time, so it comes before 去: 三点. 三个小时 is a length and cannot say when something happens.

q: 我以前学了两年游泳___，后来不学了。
zh: 我以前学了两年游泳，后来不学了。
py: wǒ yǐ qián xué le liǎng nián yóu yǒng hòu lái bù xué le
en: I studied swimming for two years before, and then I stopped.
why: 以前 and 后来 mark a stretch that is over, so there is no closing 了. A second 了 would say the two years run up to now, which contradicts 后来不学了.

zh: 他三月加入球队，训练了三个月。
py: tā sān yuè jiā rù qiú duì xùn liàn le sān gè yuè
en: He joined the team in March and trained for three months.
why: 三月 is the month he joined, so it goes before 加入; 三个月 is the length and follows 训练了. 个 shows it is a length.

q: 我昨天游了___。
zh: 我昨天游了一个小时泳。
py: wǒ zuó tiān yóu le yī gè xiǎo shí yǒng
en: I swam for an hour yesterday.
why: 游泳 is a verb plus object, so it splits around the duration: 游了一个小时泳. 游了泳一个小时 copies the English order, and 泳了 would put a second 了 where none belongs.

zh: 我去过这家店三次。
py: wǒ qù guo zhè jiā diàn sān cì
en: I've been to this shop three times.
why: With a place, the count goes on either side: 去过这家店三次 or 去过三次这家店. Both stay after 去过, and the place can also be fronted as the topic.

s: 我踢了十年足球了，现在还在踢。
zh: 我踢了十年足球了，现在还在踢。
py: wǒ tī le shí nián zú qiú le xiàn zài hái zài tī
en: I've been playing football for ten years, and I still play.
why: Correct. The double 了 is needed because the ten years are counted up to now and 现在还在踢 confirms it continues.

zh: 老师帮了我一个下午。
py: lǎo shī bāng le wǒ yī gè xià wǔ
en: The teacher helped me for a whole afternoon.
why: With the pronoun 我 as object, it follows 帮了 immediately and the duration comes last.

zh: 我五点去商场逛了一个小时。
py: wǒ wǔ diǎn qù shāng chǎng guàng le yī gè xiǎo shí
en: I went to the mall at five and walked around for an hour.
why: 五点 is a point in time, placed before the verb; 一个小时 is a length, placed after 逛了. The two are not interchangeable.

zh: 我在网上买过两次球鞋。
py: wǒ zài wǎng shàng mǎi guo liǎng cì qiú xié
en: I've bought sports shoes online twice.
why: A thing object follows the count: 买过两次球鞋. The place phrase 在网上 stays before the verb.

q: 这家球馆我去___，每次都玩得很开心。
zh: 这家球馆我去过三次，每次都玩得很开心。
py: zhè jiā qiú guǎn wǒ qù guo sān cì měi cì dōu wán de hěn kāi xīn
en: I've been to this sports hall three times, and I had fun every time.
why: The count follows the verb AND 过: 去过三次. 过 stays attached to the verb, so 三次过 and 三过次 are impossible.

s: 今天我去了一遍银行。
s_py: jīn tiān wǒ qù le yī biàn yín háng
zh: 今天我去了一趟银行。
py: jīn tiān wǒ qù le yī tàng yín háng
en: I made a trip to the bank today.
why: A journey there and back is counted with 趟. 遍 counts running through something, so 去了一遍银行 is wrong.

zh: 我每个周末打两个小时的乒乓球。
py: wǒ měi gè zhōu mò dǎ liǎng gè xiǎo shí de pīng pāng qiú
en: I play table tennis for two hours every weekend.
why: The duration plus 的 sits between the verb and its object. 每个周末 is the time frame and stays before the verb.

zh: 小王上周在家休息了三天。
py: xiǎo wáng shàng zhōu zài jiā xiū xi le sān tiān
en: Xiao Wang rested at home for three days last week.
why: 上周 is the time-when and goes before the verb phrase; 三天 is the length and follows 休息了. 三天 cannot go before 休息了.

src_py: wǒ men dōu děng le hěn jiǔ
task: Say we all waited for her (她) for a long time.
zh: 我们都等了她很久。
py: wǒ men dōu děng le tā hěn jiǔ
en: We all waited for her for a long time.
why: The pronoun 她 is inserted right after 等了 and before the duration 很久.

src: 我上个月每天都看球赛。
src_py: wǒ shàng gè yuè měi tiān dōu kàn qiú sài
task: Say you haven't watched a match for over a month.
zh: 我已经一个多月没看球赛了。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng yī gè duō yuè méi kàn qiú sài le
en: I haven't watched a match for over a month now.
why: The duration 一个多月 stands before 没 + verb, after 已经, and 了 closes the sentence because it is still true.

s: 我跟朋友打羽毛球打了一个下午。
zh: 我跟朋友打羽毛球打了一个下午。
py: wǒ gēn péng you dǎ yǔ máo qiú dǎ le yī gè xià wǔ
en: I played badminton with friends all afternoon.
why: Correct. Verb-copy repeats 打, with 了 and the duration on the second one. It looks odd to English speakers but is the normal form.

zh: 他买衣服买了一个下午。
py: tā mǎi yī fu mǎi le yī gè xià wǔ
en: He spent the whole afternoon buying clothes.
why: 买衣服 is repeated: the object phrase first, then 买了 with the duration. 了 follows the second 买 only.

zh: 他因为工作忙两个月没去健身房了。
py: tā yīn wèi gōng zuò máng liǎng gè yuè méi qù jiàn shēn fáng le
en: Because work has been busy, he hasn't been to the gym for two months.
why: The reason clause comes first, then the duration, then 没 + verb, and a final 了. The duration cannot be put after 去 or after 健身房.

zh: 他每天跑半个小时。
py: tā měi tiān pǎo bàn gè xiǎo shí
en: He runs for half an hour every day.
why: 每天 says when and stays before the verb; 半个小时 says how long and follows 跑. A habit takes no 了.

zh: 他踢足球踢了三个小时。
py: tā tī zú qiú tī le sān gè xiǎo shí
en: He played football for three hours.
why: Verb-copy: the verb with its object comes first, then the verb again with 了 and the duration. 了 goes on the second verb only.

s: 他两个小时在球场上练了。
s_py: tā liǎng gè xiǎo shí zài qiú chǎng shàng liàn le
zh: 他在球场上练了两个小时。
py: tā zài qiú chǎng shàng liàn le liǎng gè xiǎo shí
en: He practised on the court for two hours.
why: How long goes after the verb and 了. In front of the verb it would need 就 and mean 'within two hours', so 两个小时在球场上练了 is wrong.

q: 我___了，这件还是去年买的。
zh: 我半年没买新衣服了，这件还是去年买的。
py: wǒ bàn nián méi mǎi xīn yī fu le zhè jiàn hái shi qù nián mǎi de
en: I haven't bought new clothes for half a year. This one is still from last year.
why: The duration of not buying goes before 没 (半年没买), with 了 closing the sentence. 没买半年新衣服 copies English and is not used.

s: 我今年去过上海两次，都没时间逛街。
zh: 我今年去过上海两次，都没时间逛街。
py: wǒ jīn nián qù guo shàng hǎi liǎng cì dōu méi shí jiān guàng jiē
en: I've been to Shanghai twice this year and had no time to go shopping either time.
why: Correct. A place name allows the count on either side: 去过上海两次 equals 去过两次上海.

zh: 他们昨天在体育馆训练了整整四个小时。
py: tā men zuó tiān zài tǐ yù guǎn xùn liàn le zhěng zhěng sì gè xiǎo shí
en: They trained at the gym for a full four hours yesterday.
why: 四个小时 follows 训练了 as the length. 整整 may sit right before the number or before the verb; 昨天 and 在体育馆 stay before the verb.

q: 我们___了，今天一起打场球吧。
zh: 我们两个月没打球了，今天一起打场球吧。
py: wǒ men liǎng gè yuè méi dǎ qiú le jīn tiān yī qǐ dǎ chǎng qiú ba
en: We haven't played ball for two months. Let's have a game together today.
why: For 'haven't done it for two months' the duration comes before 没: 两个月没打球了. 没打两个月球 puts it after the verb, which is the English order.

q: 我练了___，身体好多了。
zh: 我练了半年瑜伽，身体好多了。
py: wǒ liàn le bàn nián yú jiā shēn tǐ hǎo duō le
en: I've practised yoga for half a year, and I feel much better.
why: The duration goes between 练了 and the object: 练了半年瑜伽. 练了瑜伽半年 puts it after the object as in English, and 了 cannot appear twice.

s: 去年他有三个月没打球，所以现在跑不快。
zh: 去年他有三个月没打球，所以现在跑不快。
py: qù nián tā yǒu sān gè yuè méi dǎ qiú suǒ yǐ xiàn zài pǎo bú kuài
en: Last year he didn't play ball for three months, so now he can't run fast.
why: Correct. 有三个月 comes before 没打球, the same 'duration before the negative' order, here without a final 了 because it is a past stretch.

s: 他今年生过三次病。
s_py: tā jīn nián shēng guo sān cì bìng
zh: 他今年生过三次病。
py: tā jīn nián shēng guo sān cì bìng
en: He has been ill three times this year.
why: Correct. 生病 is a verb plus object, so 过 and the count go in the middle: 生过三次病. Learners expect 生病过三次, which is heard but is not the pattern to learn.

s: 我们明天两个小时打球。
s_py: wǒ men míng tiān liǎng gè xiǎo shí dǎ qiú
zh: 我们明天打两个小时球。
py: wǒ men míng tiān dǎ liǎng gè xiǎo shí qiú
en: We'll play ball for two hours tomorrow.
why: 明天 is when and goes before the verb; 两个小时 is how long and goes after it. A length before the verb cannot give the duration of playing.

s: 我们在球场边休息一会儿吧。
zh: 我们在球场边休息一会儿吧。
py: wǒ men zài qiú chǎng biān xiū xi yī huì r ba
en: Let's rest by the court for a while.
why: Correct. 一会儿 is a length of time and follows the verb 休息.

q: 上个月他给我打了___，都是问球票的事。
zh: 上个月他给我打了三次电话，都是问球票的事。
py: shàng gè yuè tā gěi wǒ dǎ le sān cì diàn huà dōu shì wèn qiú piào de shì
en: Last month he phoned me three times, always about match tickets.
why: A thing object (电话) comes after the count: 打了三次电话. 打了电话三次 puts the count last as English does.

q: 上个月他在体育馆练了三个星期拳击___，后来受伤了。
zh: 上个月他在体育馆练了三个星期拳击，后来受伤了。
py: shàng gè yuè tā zài tǐ yù guǎn liàn le sān gè xīng qī quán jī hòu lái shòu shāng le
en: Last month he trained boxing at the gym for three weeks, and then he got injured.
why: The three weeks ended when he was injured (后来受伤了), so one 了 after the verb is enough. A second 了 would say the training is still going on.

src_py: jiào liàn biǎo yáng guo wǒ
task: Say the coach has praised me three times.
zh: 教练表扬过我三次。
py: jiào liàn biǎo yáng guo wǒ sān cì
en: The coach has praised me three times.
why: The pronoun 我 stays right after 表扬过 and the count 三次 follows it.

s: 我很久没逛街了，今天想多买几件。
zh: 我很久没逛街了，今天想多买几件。
py: wǒ hěn jiǔ méi guàng jiē le jīn tiān xiǎng duō mǎi jǐ jiàn
en: I haven't been shopping for a long time. Today I want to buy a few more things.
why: Correct. 很久 is a duration and goes before 没, with 了 at the end because it is still true now.

zh: 这首歌我听了五遍。
py: zhè shǒu gē wǒ tīng le wǔ biàn
en: I listened to this song five times.
why: The count 五遍 comes after 听了, and 遍 fits because the song is heard from start to finish. 五遍听了 puts the count in front of the verb.

src_py: tā xué le sān gè yuè yóu yǒng
task: Say she hasn't been swimming for three months.
zh: 她三个月没游泳了。
py: tā sān gè yuè méi yóu yǒng le
en: She hasn't been swimming for three months.
why: When the action does not happen, the duration moves in front of 没, and the sentence ends in 了.

s: 上个月我学了三天太极拳了，后来就放弃了。
s_py: shàng gè yuè wǒ xué le sān tiān tài jí quán le hòu lái jiù fàng qì le
zh: 上个月我学了三天太极拳，后来就放弃了。
py: shàng gè yuè wǒ xué le sān tiān tài jí quán hòu lái jiù fàng qì le
en: Last month I learned tai chi for three days and then gave up.
why: The three days ended when I gave up (后来就放弃了), so only one 了 follows the verb. A final 了 says the learning is still going on.

q: 这个月他请___，教练有点不高兴。
zh: 这个月他请了三次假，教练有点不高兴。
py: zhè gè yuè tā qǐng le sān cì jià jiào liàn yǒu diǎn bù gāo xìng
en: He took leave three times this month, and the coach is a little unhappy.
why: 请假 is a verb plus object, so 了 and the count go in the middle: 请了三次假. 了假三次 cuts the word apart in the wrong place, and 三次了假 detaches 了 from the verb.

q: 我在商店门口等了___。
zh: 我在商店门口等了他半个小时。
py: wǒ zài shāng diàn mén kǒu děng le tā bàn gè xiǎo shí
en: I waited for him at the shop entrance for half an hour.
why: A pronoun object comes straight after 等了, before the duration. 半个小时他 is the English order, and 的 never links a duration to a pronoun.

zh: 他这个星期迟到了三次。
py: tā zhè gè xīng qī chí dào le sān cì
en: He was late three times this week.
why: The period 这个星期 goes before the verb, while the count 三次 follows 迟到了. 三次迟到了 puts the count in the time-when slot.

zh: 他每天要来回跑两趟。
py: tā měi tiān yào lái huí pǎo liǎng tàng
en: He has to make two round trips every day.
why: 趟 counts trips there and back and follows the verb. 每天 is the period and stays before the verb, just as 来回 stays with it.

q: 我陪了___，帮她挑了三双跑鞋。
zh: 我陪了她一个下午，帮她挑了三双跑鞋。
py: wǒ péi le tā yī gè xià wǔ bāng tā tiāo le sān shuāng pǎo xié
en: I kept her company for the whole afternoon and helped her pick three pairs of running shoes.
why: 陪 takes the person right after 了, and the length of time comes after the person: 陪了她一个下午. A duration in front of 她, with or without 的, is wrong.

q: 他每天都要骑一个小时___自行车。
zh: 他每天都要骑一个小时的自行车。
py: tā měi tiān dōu yào qí yī gè xiǎo shí de zì xíng chē
en: He rides a bicycle for an hour every day.
why: With a thing object, 的 can link the duration to the object: 一个小时的自行车. 了 would make it a finished event, which clashes with 每天都要 (a habit), and 着 / 过 do not link a duration to a noun.

q: 我们在朋友的婚礼上只见过___，还不太熟。
zh: 我们在朋友的婚礼上只见过一次面，还不太熟。
py: wǒ men zài péng you de hūn lǐ shàng zhǐ jiàn guo yī cì miàn hái bú tài shú
en: We've only met once, at a friend's wedding, so we don't know each other well yet.
why: 见面 is a verb-object word and splits around the count: 见过一次面. 见过面一次 leaves the count behind the object 面, which does not work.

zh: 我们早上七点爬山，爬了三个小时。
py: wǒ men zǎo shang qī diǎn pá shān pá le sān gè xiǎo shí
en: We went hiking at seven in the morning and climbed for three hours.
why: 早上七点 is when, so it sits before 爬山; 三个小时 is how long, so it follows the second 爬了.

q: 我们昨天逛街逛___一个下午，什么也没买。
zh: 我们昨天逛街逛了一个下午，什么也没买。
py: wǒ men zuó tiān guàng jiē guàng le yī gè xià wǔ shén me yě méi mǎi
en: We spent all yesterday afternoon shopping and bought nothing.
why: In the verb-copy form, 了 goes on the second 逛, right before the duration. 过 would mean a general experience, which does not fit the one day 昨天.

src_py: tā zǎo shang qī diǎn qù pǎo bù
task: Say he ran for an hour in the morning.
zh: 他早上跑了一个小时。
py: tā zǎo shang pǎo le yī gè xiǎo shí
en: He ran for an hour in the morning.
why: The point in time (七点) becomes a length (一个小时) and moves after the verb; 早上 stays before.

zh: 妈妈在医院照顾了他三个星期。
py: mā ma zài yī yuàn zhào gù le tā sān gè xīng qī
en: Mum looked after him in the hospital for three weeks.
why: The pronoun 他 sits between 照顾了 and 三个星期. The place 在医院 stays before the verb.

q: 他们已经打了___，现在还在打。
zh: 他们已经打了一个小时篮球了，现在还在打。
py: tā men yǐ jīng dǎ le yī gè xiǎo shí lán qiú le xiàn zài hái zài dǎ
en: They have already been playing basketball for an hour, and they're still playing.
why: Still going on calls for a second 了 at the very end, after the object. A 了 between the duration and the object, or a doubled 了 after 打, breaks the pattern.

src_py: wǒ liàn le yī nián jí tā
task: Say you have been practising for a year and still are.
zh: 我练了一年吉他了。
py: wǒ liàn le yī nián jí tā le
en: I've been practising the guitar for a year now.
why: A second 了 at the end of the sentence shows the year is counted up to now and the practice goes on.

q: 教练教了___，我们才学会游泳。
zh: 教练教了我们三个月，我们才学会游泳。
py: jiào liàn jiāo le wǒ men sān gè yuè wǒ men cái xué huì yóu yǒng
en: The coach taught us for three months before we learned to swim.
why: The pronoun 我们 goes right after 教了 and before 三个月. Putting the duration first, with or without 的, is not Chinese.

q: 这家店开业十年___，老顾客特别多。
zh: 这家店开业十年了，老顾客特别多。
py: zhè jiā diàn kāi yè shí nián le lǎo gù kè tè bié duō
en: This shop has been open for ten years, and it has lots of regulars.
why: 开业 starts at one moment, so the time since then follows it and the clause ends in 了, counting up to now. 过, 着 and 的 cannot close this pattern.

s: 妈妈找了一个小时的你。
s_py: mā ma zhǎo le yī gè xiǎo shí de nǐ
zh: 妈妈找了你一个小时。
py: mā ma zhǎo le nǐ yī gè xiǎo shí
en: Mum looked for you for an hour.
why: With 你, the pronoun comes before the duration, and 的 cannot join them. 一个小时的你 is wrong.

zh: 我三天没跑步了。
py: wǒ sān tiān méi pǎo bù le
en: I haven't gone running for three days.
why: The period of not doing something goes before 没; 了 at the end says it is still true. 没跑步三天 leaves the duration after a verb that did not happen.

q: 受伤以后他___，所以朋友们都很担心。
zh: 受伤以后他一个星期没出门，所以朋友们都很担心。
py: shòu shāng yǐ hòu tā yī gè xīng qī méi chū mén suǒ yǐ péng you men dōu hěn dān xīn
en: After he got hurt, he didn't go out for a week, so his friends were worried.
why: He did not go out for a week: the week goes before 没, and the verb-object 出门 stays together. 没出一个星期门 splits 出门 and leaves the duration behind 没.

zh: 他周末踢了两个小时球。
py: tā zhōu mò tī le liǎng gè xiǎo shí qiú
en: He played ball for two hours at the weekend.
why: 两个小时 goes between 踢了 and 球, as for any thing object. 周末 is when and goes before the verb.
